title: segresearch: where byte-level language models should start their patches
description:
Code, logs and results for two papers on where byte-level language models should start their patches: Easy to anticipate, hard to compute: boundary dependence finds the computed outputs that entropy patching misses (arXiv:2610.11790) and When the next byte's type is fixed: why entropy patching skips computed values under tight budgets (arXiv:2610.22100, version 2). Byte-level language models such as BLT start a patch where next-byte entropy is high; under tight budgets this skips positions whose type the preceding text fixes but whose value must be computed, such as the number after '=' in a worked math solution. The repository contains the BLT-style training harness (MLX, and a PyTorch port verified against it), the experiments on Meta's BLT-1B (with the upstream fix for the 512-byte attention window of the Hugging Face conversion), the scaling study at 1M-50M parameters, the results registry with per-target outputs, the support files of both papers' version 2 (paper/v2/, paper2/v2/), and the scripts that regenerate every table, figure and tested number.

Datasets (GSM8K, MATH, OpenWebMath) and the BLT-1B weights are not redistributed; the scripts download them from their sources. The exceptions are GSM8K-derived texts under GSM8K's MIT licence: LLM-written prose rewrites of GSM8K problems (paper/v2/data/, paper2/v2/data/) and the copy-test texts built from GSM8K train problems (paper2/v2/data/copy_latch_texts/).
